name: EZSnsRF
description: A plug-in receiver that turns codes from Dakota Alert 3000-series wireless transmitters, such as motion, driveway, contact and liquid sensors, into Insteon scene commands, for up to 20 scenes.

steps.text: Choose a power outlet anywhere on the Insteon powerline network, away from moisture, where the receiver can stand vertically clear of metal obstructions. Outdoors, use an approved weatherproof enclosure.
Plug the EZSnsRF into the outlet.
steps.expect: Status LED flashes a number of times, then glows steadily after a few seconds

steps.text: Set each wireless transmitter's 10 DIP switches, on (up) or off (down), to give it a code of its own.
Press and hold the SET button for about 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED flashes about once a second

steps.text: Activate the wireless transmitter to be learned, such as by passing in front of a motion sensor or pressing its transmit button.
Press and hold the SET button of the device to be controlled until its LED blinks, about 4 seconds.
steps.expect: The device's LED blinks; the EZSnsRF's LED may flash briefly, then keeps blinking about twice a second

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
To add an Off delay, tap the SET button 1 to 31 times; each tap adds half a minute, from 0.5 to 15.5 minutes.
Press and hold the SET button for 4 seconds to end the linking session.

notes: This learns a transmitter's code and links responders to it as the code's scene. Repeat the step on the device to be controlled for each further device before ending the session.

Without an Off delay, skip the taps. The Quick-Start Guide EZSnsRF Wireless Sensor Receiver Model #5010E conflicts with itself on how to finish then: its step 5 ends the linking session with a 4-second hold of the SET button, and its note says to tap the SET button once more to finish. The steps follow the 4-second hold.
Pressing and holding the SET button for 4 seconds cancels the process at any step.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for about 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED flashes about once a second

steps.text: Activate the wireless transmitter to be learned, such as by passing in front of a motion sensor or pressing its transmit button.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
To add an Off delay, tap the SET button 1 to 31 times; each tap adds half a minute, from 0.5 to 15.5 minutes.
Press and hold the SET button for 4 seconds to end the linking session.
Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the EZSnsRF's group for the transmitter's code to the Hub as a controller, with the Hub as the responder, so the Hub receives the group command for the learned code; the Hub makes no link to the device, since this profile lists no group it responds to.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps, with the Hub in place of the device to be controlled, and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Unplug the EZSnsRF.
Wait at least 5 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button while plugging it back in.
Keep holding the SET button for 5 seconds more.
Release the SET button.

notes: Erases all programming and restores the factory defaults.

steps.text: Remove the device as a controller from each of its responders.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 set to the group linked to the Hub, such as 0x01 for group 1.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode and Start ALL-Linking; no document describes removing this product from a Hub. The EZSnsRF Insteon Messages/Commands give Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with the group number in cmd2.

notes: Dakota Alert 3000-series transmitters reach up to 600 feet. The EZSnsRF has a pass-through outlet, which shouldn't power anything that emits radio signals.
The commands each code sends when its signal turns on and off are programmable, so no document gives them.
The Quick-Start Guide EZSnsRF Wireless Sensor Receiver Model #5010E (Rev 1.5) applies to firmware 1.6 and above.
